scenarios.title: Phishing

attack.name: Spearphishing Link
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enforce DMARC with SPF and DKIM, inspect URLs, and require phishing-resistant authentication.

scenarios.title: MFA Fatigue

attack.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Require phishing-resistant MFA where possible. Enable number matching and authentication throttling for remaining push users.

scenarios.title: Password Spraying

attack.name: Password Spraying
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use phishing-resistant MFA, adaptive access, smart lockout and monitored legacy protocol controls.

scenarios.title: Public-Facing Application Exploits

attack.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Reduce exposure, maintain a patch SLA and monitor WAF policy changes.

scenarios.title: OAuth Consent Phishing

attack.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack.rationale: Risky consent may enable theft or misuse of application access tokens. A consent event alone does not demonstrate token theft.

scenarios.defensive_control: Require administrator review for sensitive consent and audit privileged delegated scopes.

scenarios.title: PowerShell Abuse

attack.name: PowerShell
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enable script block logging, AMSI integration and application control. Review Office child-process policy.

scenarios.title: HTML Smuggling

attack.name: HTML Smuggling
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Apply HTML attachment controls, approved sandboxes and browser download policy.

scenarios.title: Scheduled Tasks/Cron

attack.name: Cron
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Restrict cron directory writes and monitor job definitions and changes.

scenarios.title: Registry Autoruns

attack.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Keep a software and autorun baseline, restrict execution from user-writable paths and monitor registry change events.

scenarios.title: WMI Subscription

attack.name: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Collect WMI activity and monitor changes to permanent subscriptions on high-value hosts.

scenarios.title: Token Theft

attack.name: Application Access Token
attack.rationale: Observed reuse can be consistent with application token abuse. It does not establish how the token was obtained.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enforce phishing-resistant authentication, managed device policy and token binding where supported.

scenarios.title: Credential Dumping

attack.name: LSASS Memory
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enable Credential Guard and LSASS protection where appropriate and audit their status.

scenarios.title: Kerberoasting

attack.name: Kerberoasting
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Prefer gMSAs and modern encryption. Audit service principal assignments and legacy-client dependencies.

scenarios.title: Pass-the-Hash

attack.name: Pass the Hash
attack.rationale: An anomalous NTLM logon is compatible with pass-the-hash, but the authentication record does not identify credential form.

scenarios.defensive_control: Roll out unique managed local administrator passwords, restrict NTLM and segment administration traffic.

scenarios.title: Privilege Escalation

attack.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack.rationale: Unexpected elevation motivates a T1068 investigation. A privilege transition can have other causes.

scenarios.defensive_control: Patch OS and packages, constrain privilege brokers and review privileged execution policies.

scenarios.title: RDP/SMB/WinRM Abuse

attack.name: Remote Services
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Require segmented management paths, MFA for remote access and monitored privileged accounts.

scenarios.title: LOLBins/LOLBAS

attack.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use application control and audit document applications that launch child processes.

scenarios.title: Disable Security Tools

attack.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enable tamper protection and retain service and security logs off the endpoint.

scenarios.title: HTTPS/DNS Command & Control

attack.name: DNS
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use controlled resolvers, egress filtering and DNS analytics with reviewed allowlists.

scenarios.title: Cloud IAM Abuse

attack.name: Additional Cloud Roles
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enforce least privilege, short-lived roles and change approval for administrative grants.

scenarios.title: Active Directory Enumeration

attack.name: Domain Account
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Audit directory queries for sensitive objects and reduce the reach of unmanaged directory clients.

scenarios.title: Cloud Exfiltration

attack.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack.rationale: T1530 describes collection from cloud storage. External transfer requires additional evidence.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enable object-level audit for restricted storage, scope access and enforce approved destinations.

scenarios.title: Ransomware-Like Activity

attack.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack.rationale: Mass renames can be consistent with encryption for impact. Rename evidence alone does not show that content was encrypted.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use offline tested backups, application control, staged share permissions and fast endpoint isolation procedures.

scenarios.title: Data Staging

attack.name: Archive via Utility
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Limit staging access, use DLP and monitor outbound transfers from systems with sensitive datasets.

scenarios.title: Wiper-Like Activity

attack.name: Data Destruction
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Protect backups from the same identity plane and require review for large destructive changes.

scenarios.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing

attack.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack.rationale: Session drift supports a relay hypothesis. It does not directly show that an adversary intercepted traffic.

scenarios.defensive_control: Require origin-bound authentication such as FIDO2 passkeys and apply conditional access to session risk.

scenarios.title: Device-Code Phishing

attack.name: Spearphishing Link
attack.rationale: T1566.002 represents link-based phishing delivery that can lead to a device grant. The fixture observes the grant only.

scenarios.defensive_control: Limit device authorization flow to approved applications with conditional access and user education.

scenarios.title: Browser Cookie Theft

attack.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Restrict process access, enforce session protections and monitor browser profile access.

scenarios.title: Infostealers

attack.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Apply endpoint hardening, managed browser policy and monitored credential-store access.

scenarios.title: QR-Code Phishing

attack.name: Spearphishing Link
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use QR inspection and phishing-resistant authentication. Teach users to report unexpected QR sign-in prompts.

scenarios.title: Malicious Dependencies

attack.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use dependency review, pinned lockfiles, restricted install scripts and verified provenance.

scenarios.title: CI/CD Token Compromise

attack.name: Application Access Token
attack.rationale: T1550.001 applies to use of an application access token. The sample does not show theft itself.

scenarios.defensive_control: Prefer short-lived workload identity and narrowly scoped job tokens. Require approved runner images and pools.

scenarios.title: GitHub Actions Tampering

attack.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
attack.rationale: A risky workflow edit can set up poisoned pipeline execution. The fixture records a configuration change without executing a job.

scenarios.defensive_control: Protect workflow paths with CODEOWNERS and required review. Set least-privilege and explicit workflow permissions.

scenarios.title: Secrets in Git/Artifacts

attack.name: Credentials In Files
attack.rationale: Credentials in Files models discovery of credentials in files. The lab detects potential exposure only.

scenarios.defensive_control: Run secret scanning before release and use short-lived credentials or workload identity.

scenarios.title: Kubernetes RBAC Abuse

attack.name: Additional Container Cluster Roles
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use least-privilege RBAC, change review for privileged bindings, and admission controls where appropriate.

scenarios.title: Container Escape

attack.name: Escape to Host
attack.rationale: The exercise observes a risky configuration associated with potential escape. It does not reproduce escape or prove it occurred.

scenarios.defensive_control: Use Pod Security Standards, scoped admission exceptions and independent runtime monitoring.

scenarios.title: Cloud Metadata Credential Theft

attack.name: Cloud Instance Metadata API
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Require IMDSv2 where supported, constrain metadata access and limit instance-role privileges.

scenarios.title: BYOVD Driver Abuse

attack.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack.rationale: Driver vulnerability can be relevant to privilege escalation. The fixture does not establish driver exploitation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Enforce recommended vulnerable driver blocklists, HVCI where supported, and update drivers from trusted sources.

scenarios.title: RMM Tool Abuse

attack.name: Remote Desktop Software
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

scenarios.defensive_control: Allow approved support tools only, require MFA and maintain an inventory of remote-access agents.

scenarios.title: SaaS Exfiltration

attack.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack.rationale: External sharing can provide a route for exfiltration over a web service. The fixture represents sharing and not confirmed download.

scenarios.defensive_control: Apply DLP, external sharing policy, data classification and conditional access.
